headline: Malaysia-bound workers’ medical tests to cost Tk 8,000
summary: The expatriates’ welfare ministry has set a fixed fee for medical examinations for workers seeking employment in Malaysia. It has warned medical centres against charging more than the prescribed amount.
details: Bangladeshi workers aspiring to work in Malaysia will now have to pay a fixed fee of Tk 8,000 for their mandatory medical examinations. The expatriates’ welfare ministry announced this new regulation, aiming to standardize the process and prevent overcharging.

The ministry has issued a stern warning to all medical centres involved in the pre-departure health checks, explicitly stating that they are prohibited from collecting any amount exceeding the set Tk 8,000. Furthermore, it has advised workers against engaging with brokers or intermediaries for arranging their medical tests, emphasizing a direct and transparent process.

To ensure fairness and prevent monopolies, the ministry has stipulated that no medical centre will operate under the exclusive authority of a specific recruiting agency. Workers selected for jobs in Malaysia will have the freedom to choose any approved medical centre for their examinations. The ministry also stated that if a worker opts for a different medical centre than the one initially suggested by the recruiting agency, the original agency must promptly transfer the medical report without any objections.

The ministry has provided an official email address (secretary@probashi.gov.bd) for workers to report any medical centre that demands more than the fixed fee, causes harassment, or creates undue delays. Regular monitoring and inspections of these medical facilities will be conducted to ensure strict adherence to the new regulations. Legal action will be pursued against any centre found to be involved in irregularities.

This development follows the government's announcement on October 15 that the recruitment of Bangladeshi workers for Malaysia would resume. Malaysia had agreed in principle to accept 10,000 Bangladeshi workers with no associated costs for the workers themselves, and also agreed to include 338 Bangladeshi recruiting agencies in the process.

headline_marked: Tk 30,000 wage demand: [[RMG workers block roads]] in Mirpur
headline: Tk 30,000 wage demand: RMG workers block roads in Mirpur
summary: Hundreds of garment workers protested in Dhaka's Mirpur area for hours, causing severe traffic congestion across multiple intersections.
details: Hundreds of readymade garment (RMG) workers blocked several roads in Dhaka’s Mirpur area for around four hours today, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.

The protests began around 10:45 am, disrupting traffic in Mirpur-10, Mirpur-11, Mirpur-12, and around the Proshika intersection, according to the Mirpur Traffic Division of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police.
While some roads were cleared by 2:30 pm, protesters continued to block roads at Mirpur-11.5 and Kalshi as of 3:00 pm.
Commuters faced significant delays, with some buses forced to take detours through Hallpotti to bypass the congestion.
Workers cited a sharp decline in purchasing power due to rising costs of essentials and high house rents as the primary reason for their demands.
One worker shared that despite earning Tk 18,000 to Tk 20,000 including overtime, a large portion goes toward rent, making it impossible to survive on the remainder.
Factory owners urged workers to return to work, stating that wage discussions are ongoing with foreign buyers, the BGMEA, and government officials.
Protesters, however, rejected verbal assurances, vowing to continue their protests until a wage hike is officially announced.
Similar protests occurred in Mirpur earlier on Thursday and in Uttara for several days, some of which escalated into clashes with police.
